fee.label: Tuition (non-EU)
fee.contributionUnknown: Not verified — the amount is published on the institution's website.
fee.explainTuition: Tuition is a fee for teaching charged to some students (here: non-EU citizens).
fee.explainContribution: The semester contribution is paid by every student each semester (student services, student union, often a transport ticket). It is not tuition.
fee.explainLiving: Living costs (rent, food, insurance) are separate from both.
fee.excludesTicket: No transport ticket included in this amount.
fee.explainFirstEnrolment: At first enrolment some universities add small one-off charges, such as a student ID card.

detail.programsIntro: Programmes Studiva highlights for this institution. This is not the complete list.
detail.programsCatalog: Search all programmes in the DAAD International Programmes database or on the official website.

admissionGuidance.Universität: Bachelor's applicants from Turkey typically need a recognised school-leaving certificate plus, in many cases, university study in Turkey or a foundation year (Studienkolleg), proof of language skills and an APS certificate. Master's applicants need a relevant first degree.
admissionGuidance.Fachhochschule: Universities of applied sciences have similar formal requirements to universities; some programmes add practical-experience requirements. Bachelor's applicants from Turkey often need an APS certificate and proof of language skills.
admissionGuidance.Duale Hochschule: Dual study combines study with paid work at a partner company: you usually need a training contract with a company before you can enrol.

detail.languageGuidance: German-taught programmes usually ask for DSH-2, TestDaF 4×4 or equivalent; English-taught programmes usually ask for IELTS or TOEFL. Exact scores are set per programme.
detail.scholarshipsBody: See established scholarship programmes open to international students, and check this institution's own scholarships on its website.
detail.uniAssistMember: This institution is a uni-assist member. Many — not necessarily all — of its programmes accept international applications through uni-assist.
detail.uniAssistUnknown: We have not verified whether this institution uses uni-assist. Check the programme page for the application route.
detail.applyChecklist: Check the programme page for the application portal, deadline and required documents for your applicant category.
detail.factsVsGuidance: Items marked “Official source” link to the page we checked. Items marked “Studiva guidance” are our general advice.
detail.daadCount: DAAD lists {total, plural, one {# degree programme} other {# degree programmes}} here — {english} taught fully or partly in English.
detail.daadSplit: Including {bachelor} bachelor's and {master} master's programmes in English.
detail.daadNote: Counts from DAAD's International Programmes database, fetched {date}. It lists international programmes only, so the university may offer more. Links open DAAD's official search.
detail.uniAssistNonMember: This institution is not a uni-assist member, so international applications usually go directly to the university through its own portal. Check the programme page for the exact route.
detail.hskCount: The HRK Higher Education Compass lists {total, plural, one {# degree programme} other {# degree programmes}} here.
detail.hskEnglish: {count, plural, one {# is} other {# are}} taught in English.
detail.hskNote: Counts from the HRK Higher Education Compass via DAAD, fetched {date}. Studiva groups its fields of study into the subject areas above. Links open the official search.

finder.title: University finder
finder.subtitle: Answer a few questions and get a shortlist from our verified data — with the reasons each university does or doesn't match.
finder.howBody: Each answer is a criterion. A criterion is “met” only when our data confirms it, “not met” when our data contradicts it, and “unknown” when we have not verified it. There is no hidden score.

questions.subject: Which subject area interests you?

results.possibleNote: Nothing contradicts your answers, but some criteria are unverified.

states.title: Explore Germany by state
states.subtitle: Germany has 16 federal states, and higher-education policy — including tuition for non-EU students — is set at state level. Browse the states, their university cities and the institutions in our directory.
states.universities: {count, plural, =0 {No universities in our directory} one {# university in our directory} other {# universities in our directory}}
states.coverage: Our directory lists {count} institutions in this state — not every higher-education institution there.
states.costsBody: Germany-wide reference: students spend {total} per month on average, of which {rent} on rent (DZHW 22nd Social Survey, published by DAAD). Costs are higher in large cities — use the cost calculator with your own figures.
states.multiCampusNote: Listed under its legal seat; it also runs campuses in other states.

costs.title: Study cost calculator
costs.subtitle: Estimate your monthly and annual costs in Germany. Defaults come from published national averages — replace them with your own numbers.
costs.disclaimer: This is a planning aid, not an official financial assessment. Visa requirements and real costs depend on your city, programme and circumstances.
costs.tuitionHint: Most public universities charge no tuition, but Baden-Württemberg, some Bavarian institutions and private universities do. Fees depend on the institution, programme and your nationality.
costs.tuitionRangeFromUni: {name}: {range} per semester depending on programme — enter the figure for your programme.
costs.contributionHint: Paid by every student each semester; check your university's website for the exact amount.
costs.method: Method: monthly items × 12 + (tuition + semester contribution) × 2 semesters. Monthly total spreads semester fees over 6 months.
costs.visaBody: For a student visa you must show {month} per month ({year} per year), typically via a blocked account. This is a legal minimum for the visa, not an estimate of your real costs.
costs.sourceSurvey: Average student spending by item: DZHW 22nd Social Survey, as published by DAAD (checked {date}).
costs.sourceVisa: Proof of funds: DAAD, amount valid as of 1 January 2025 (checked {date}).

programmes.title: Find study programmes
programmes.subtitle: Search Germany's two official programme databases: the HRK Higher Education Compass, with every degree programme, and DAAD's International Programmes. Studiva prepares the search; the results open on DAAD's website.
programmes.keywordHint: Both databases are searched in English, so English keywords work best.
programmes.opensNote: Opens DAAD's official programme search in a new tab.
programmes.howBody: DAAD, the German Academic Exchange Service, runs the official database of international programmes in Germany — mostly taught in English — with entry requirements, deadlines and fees for each one.
programmes.whyLink: We send you to these databases instead of copying their records: programme details change often, and they are updated at the source.
programmes.listIntro: How many degree programmes the Higher Education Compass lists for each university in our directory, and how many DAAD lists as taught fully or partly in English.
programmes.fetched: Higher Education Compass counts fetched {hskDate}; DAAD counts fetched {daadDate}.
programmes.notListed: No programmes matched in DAAD's database for: {names}. Check their own websites.
programmes.databaseAllHint: HRK Higher Education Compass — every programme at state-recognised institutions.
programmes.databaseInternationalHint: DAAD — mostly English-taught, with details for international applicants.
programmes.howAll: The Higher Education Compass of the German Rectors' Conference (HRK) lists every degree programme at state-recognised universities — about 22,500 — including those taught in German.
